mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met over a 10-year sample.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of quarters when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase above 0.4 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in periods when this trigger is met (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of such episodes over a 15-year sample.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases risk premia and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month moving averages in at least 70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of such co-activation episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which raises wage inflation and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes over a 30-year sample.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates weakening residential investment, which reduces GDP growth and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of such episodes.
